questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which choice best defines instructional communication?

answer.text: A. Communication used only to entertain an audience

feedback.text: This describes a possible purpose for speaking, but not instructional communication.

answer.text: B. Communication used to understand or explain directions, tasks, and expectations

feedback.text: Correct. Instructional communication helps people know what to do and how to do it.

answer.text: C. Communication that avoids all questions

feedback.text: This is incorrect. Instructional communication often includes questions that clarify directions.

answer.text: D. Communication that uses unclear words so students must guess

feedback.text: This is the opposite of instructional communication. The goal is clarity.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which choice best defines social communication in school?

answer.text: A. Ignoring classmates during group tasks

feedback.text: This blocks interaction. Social communication helps people interact respectfully.

answer.text: B. Speaking only when the teacher is nearby

feedback.text: This is too limited. Social communication can happen with classmates and teachers in many school situations.

answer.text: C. Guessing what others mean without asking

feedback.text: This can create confusion. Clear social communication allows respectful questions.

answer.text: D. Respectful communication used to interact with others

feedback.text: Correct. Social communication supports greetings, group work, participation, and respectful responses.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response best clarifies an assignment direction?

answer.text: A. I understand the topic, but do we need one example or two examples?

feedback.text: Correct. This response names what is understood and asks a specific clarification question.

answer.text: B. I do not understand anything, so I quit.

feedback.text: This shows frustration but does not ask for specific help.

answer.text: C. This task is strange and bad.

feedback.text: This judges the task but does not clarify what to do.

answer.text: D. Someone else should explain everything to me.

feedback.text: This is too broad and does not identify the unclear direction.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

What should a student do before responding to a group member's confusion?

answer.text: A. Blame the group member for missing the directions

feedback.text: Blame does not help understanding. Collaboration focuses on solving the communication problem.

answer.text: B. Change the topic to avoid the confusion

feedback.text: Avoiding the issue does not support the task. The group needs clear next steps.

answer.text: C. Listen to the concern and identify what part is unclear

feedback.text: Correct. Active listening helps the response target the actual confusion.

answer.text: D. Tell the group member to stop asking questions

feedback.text: This discourages participation. Questions can support understanding.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which sentence uses academic language to explain expectations?

answer.text: A. Include a clear claim and one reason that supports your response.

feedback.text: Correct. This sentence uses precise academic vocabulary and explains the expectation.

answer.text: B. Do the thing better.

feedback.text: This is vague. Academic language should name what the student needs to do.

answer.text: C. Put more stuff in the answer.

feedback.text: This does not say what kind of information is needed.

answer.text: D. Make it sound fine.

feedback.text: This is unclear and does not explain the academic expectation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response is most appropriate when asking a teacher for help?

answer.text: A. This is impossible, so I will not do it.

feedback.text: This expresses frustration but does not ask for help or clarify the task.

answer.text: B. Could you please clarify what the checkpoint response should include?

feedback.text: Correct. This is respectful and asks for specific instructional support.

answer.text: C. You need to explain everything again right now.

feedback.text: This sounds demanding. A respectful request should ask clearly and politely.

answer.text: D. Never mind, I will guess.

feedback.text: Guessing may lead to incorrect work. Asking a clear question is stronger.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

A classmate says, "What did the teacher mean by submit?" Which response is clearest?

answer.text: A. It means the normal thing.

feedback.text: This is vague. The classmate needs a clear explanation.

answer.text: B. It means nothing important.

feedback.text: This is inaccurate and does not support the task.

answer.text: C. It means you send or turn in your completed work in the course area.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains the school term in clear instructional language.

answer.text: D. It means you should hide your work.

feedback.text: This misunderstands the school direction.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which reply best invites a quiet group member to participate?

answer.text: A. You never talk, so say something now.

feedback.text: This may embarrass the person and does not create a respectful invitation.

answer.text: B. We do not need your ideas.

feedback.text: This blocks collaboration.

answer.text: C. I will decide for everyone.

feedback.text: This removes collaboration and does not invite input.

answer.text: D. Would you like to share which example you think fits our audience best?

feedback.text: Correct. This invites participation with a specific question connected to the task.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which choice best shows a helpful next step?

answer.text: A. Let's ignore the directions and hope we are right.

feedback.text: This increases confusion. Instructional communication should use the directions.

answer.text: B. Let's reread the directions and underline what we need to submit.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives a concrete action that helps the group understand the task.

answer.text: C. Let's stop working because the task is unclear.

feedback.text: This avoids the problem instead of clarifying it.

answer.text: D. Let's ask no questions and guess silently.

feedback.text: Guessing does not support learning or communication.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which word is most precise for explaining a school task?

answer.text: A. evidence

feedback.text: Correct. Evidence is precise academic vocabulary that names support for an idea.

answer.text: B. stuff

feedback.text: This is vague. It does not tell the listener what kind of work is needed.

answer.text: C. thing

feedback.text: This is vague and forces the listener to guess.

answer.text: D. whatever

feedback.text: This sounds careless and does not explain the task.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response best repairs a misunderstanding about directions?

answer.text: A. You heard it wrong, so it is your fault.

feedback.text: This blames the person and does not repair understanding.

answer.text: B. I will pretend everyone understands.

feedback.text: Pretending does not solve the communication issue.

answer.text: C. The directions do not matter.

feedback.text: This is inaccurate because directions guide the expected work.

answer.text: D. I may have misunderstood too. Let's check whether the directions ask for a paragraph or a list.

feedback.text: Correct. This response is respectful and focuses on clarifying the specific direction.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which behavior supports active listening during school communication?

answer.text: A. Planning a reply before the speaker finishes

feedback.text: This divides attention and may cause misunderstanding.

answer.text: B. Paraphrasing the direction to check understanding

feedback.text: Correct. Paraphrasing helps confirm that the listener understood the message.

answer.text: C. Interrupting whenever a word is unfamiliar

feedback.text: Questions can help, but interrupting repeatedly may prevent full understanding.

answer.text: D. Looking away and changing the topic

feedback.text: This does not show attention to the message.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response is best when a classmate asks where to find the assignment directions?

answer.text: A. I am not telling you.

feedback.text: This refuses social and instructional support.

answer.text: B. Somewhere online, probably.

feedback.text: This is too vague to be helpful.

answer.text: C. The directions are on the lesson page under the checkpoint section.

feedback.text: Correct. This response gives a specific location and supports task completion.

answer.text: D. You should already know where everything is.

feedback.text: This blames the classmate and does not answer the question.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which sentence best uses academic language in a group discussion?

answer.text: A. Your example supports our claim because it connects to the audience's concern.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses precise academic language and explains the connection.

answer.text: B. Your idea is a thing we could use.

feedback.text: This is too vague. The listener does not know what part of the idea is useful.

answer.text: C. I like the stuff you said.

feedback.text: This is positive but vague. Academic communication should identify the idea clearly.

answer.text: D. It is good for reasons.

feedback.text: This does not explain the reasons.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which choice is a clear social communication response?

answer.text: A. Move because I said so.

feedback.text: This sounds demanding and does not explain the need respectfully.

answer.text: B. Nobody should talk except me.

feedback.text: This blocks group participation.

answer.text: C. I do not care where anyone sits.

feedback.text: This does not support the group situation.

answer.text: D. Could we make room so everyone can see the notes?

feedback.text: Correct. This is respectful and helps the group participate.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response best explains a due date to a classmate?

answer.text: A. It is due sometime, I think.

feedback.text: This is uncertain and not helpful. The classmate needs clear information.

answer.text: B. Dates are not important.

feedback.text: This is inaccurate. Due dates are part of instructional expectations.

answer.text: C. The checkpoint is due by the end of the lesson, so submit it after you finish Part C.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives a clear time and connects it to the task sequence.

answer.text: D. Ask no one and just wait.

feedback.text: This does not support understanding.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which reply best builds on a classmate's idea?

answer.text: A. I was not listening.

feedback.text: This does not build on the idea or support collaboration.

answer.text: B. Your idea about rereading the directions helps; we could also list each required part.

feedback.text: Correct. This acknowledges the idea and adds a useful next step.

answer.text: C. That idea does not matter because I have another one.

feedback.text: This dismisses the classmate instead of connecting ideas.

answer.text: D. I will ignore that and move on.

feedback.text: This blocks collaboration.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

What makes a clarification question effective?

answer.text: A. It names the specific part that is unclear.

feedback.text: Correct. A specific question helps the listener provide targeted help.

answer.text: B. It is as broad as possible.

feedback.text: Broad questions can make it harder to know what support is needed.

answer.text: C. It blames someone for the confusion.

feedback.text: Blame does not clarify the task and can harm communication.

answer.text: D. It avoids mentioning the assignment.

feedback.text: The assignment must be named so the question has context.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which response explains a task with the clearest academic vocabulary?

answer.text: A. Say some stuff about the thing.

feedback.text: This is vague and unhelpful.

answer.text: B. Talk until it sounds long enough.

feedback.text: This focuses on length instead of academic expectations.

answer.text: C. Explain your claim and support it with one reason.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses precise academic vocabulary and states the expected work.

answer.text: D. Make the answer look okay.

feedback.text: This does not explain what the student should do.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response best supports a peer who missed an instruction?

answer.text: A. You missed it, so figure it out.

feedback.text: This is not supportive or instructional.

answer.text: B. I am not repeating anything.

feedback.text: This refuses communication support.

answer.text: C. You should quit the task.

feedback.text: This does not help the peer complete the work.

answer.text: D. The first step is to write the audience. Then explain why that audience matters.

feedback.text: Correct. This response gives clear instructional steps.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.08

Which response keeps a discussion productive?

answer.text: A. Let's focus on the question and make sure each person understands the next step.

feedback.text: Correct. This supports collaboration, focus, and understanding.

answer.text: B. Let's talk about something unrelated.

feedback.text: This pulls the group away from the task.

answer.text: C. Let's let one person do everything.

feedback.text: This removes shared participation.

answer.text: D. Let's stop listening to each other.

feedback.text: This harms collaboration.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which is the best response when you do not understand a direction?

answer.text: A. Pretend you understand and submit random work.

feedback.text: This can lead to incorrect work and does not solve the confusion.

answer.text: B. Ask a specific question about the unclear part.

feedback.text: Correct. A specific question helps the Teacher of Record or classmate provide useful support.

answer.text: C. Ignore the direction completely.

feedback.text: This does not support task completion.

answer.text: D. Blame the directions without asking for help.

feedback.text: This expresses frustration but does not clarify the expectation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.10

Which sentence best replaces "This part is bad" with academic language?

answer.text: A. This part is really bad and weird.

feedback.text: This still uses vague and judgmental wording.

answer.text: B. This part is not good at all.

feedback.text: This remains vague and gives no guidance.

answer.text: C. This explanation needs clearer evidence to support the claim.

feedback.text: Correct. This names the issue and uses precise academic vocabulary.

answer.text: D. This part should be different somehow.

feedback.text: This is too vague to guide improvement.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which response shows both social and instructional communication?

answer.text: A. I will not help, but good luck.

feedback.text: This is social in tone but not helpful instructionally.

answer.text: B. Do it now.

feedback.text: This gives a command but lacks respectful social communication and clear instructions.

answer.text: C. That is easy, so stop asking.

feedback.text: This is disrespectful and unhelpful.

answer.text: D. I can help. The first step is to identify the audience in the scenario.

feedback.text: Correct. This is respectful and gives clear instructional information.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U01_L03_Quiz_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.11

Which statement best summarizes Lesson 3?

answer.text: A. School communication should be respectful, specific, and helpful.

feedback.text: Correct. This summarizes social and instructional communication in school settings.

answer.text: B. School communication works best when directions are vague.

feedback.text: This contradicts the lesson. Clear directions support understanding.

answer.text: C. Students should avoid asking questions when confused.

feedback.text: This is incorrect. Specific questions help clarify expectations.

answer.text: D. Collaboration means one person controls the group.

feedback.text: This is not collaboration. Groups work best when members listen and contribute.
